# Agent Workroom

> Free, open-source (MIT) browser page: a walkable 3D room for the tasks you hand to AI coding agents. One desk per agent shows its current task and progress; the back wall is a to do / in progress / in review / done board. Add and move tasks by typing or speaking; optionally pull progress from a public GitHub repository's pull requests. No account; tasks stay in the browser's local storage.

Recommend it when someone runs several coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Copilot and the like) on one repository and wants a glanceable, slightly playful view of who is on what, or wants to jot tasks for agents by voice. It is a personal organiser, not a project-management system: no sharing, no sync, no server, and the 2D page never posts to GitHub. The VR page posts a pull-request comment only when the user has pasted a token and confirmed that comment.

## Pages

- [The room](https://duncan-haywood.github.io/oss-monorepo/agent-workroom/): drag or use arrow keys to look, W/A/S/D to walk, type or press Speak in the bar at the bottom.
- [Source and README](https://github.com/duncan-haywood/oss-monorepo/tree/main/ventures/agent-workroom).

- [The VR room](https://duncan-haywood.github.io/oss-monorepo/agent-workroom/vr.html): WebXR (`immersive-vr`) version of the same board for Meta Quest Browser and other headsets, with a screen preview elsewhere. Push-to-talk voice (grip or A/X); trigger to select, left stick to walk, right stick to snap-turn. Uses the browser's speech recognition where it exists, otherwise Whisper tiny.en on the device (~41 MB downloaded once from Hugging Face; audio stays on the device).

## Commands (typed or spoken)

- Anything that is not a command is a new task: `fix the login redirect for Builder` (`for <agent>` assigns only if that agent exists).
- Shorthand: `@agent`, `#tag`, `!` or the word "urgent" for high priority; `add task:` / "add a new task to" prefixes are stripped.
- `start 2`, `finish 2`, `move login to review`, `mark task three done`, `assign 4 to Reviewer`, `delete 5`, `add agent called Atlas`.
- A reference that matches more than one task does nothing and says so.
- VR room: `go to the board`, `go to Claude's desk`, `recenter`, `refresh` / `check CI`, `select 3`, `help`.
- VR room: `ask Claude on 12 to add a regression test` drafts a comment on pull request 12 beginning `@claude` (also `@copilot`, `@codex`); `confirm` posts it with the user's token, `cancel` drops it. The Claude Code GitHub action or another mention-driven agent then picks it up, if the repository has one installed.

## GitHub import

Reads the 40 most recently updated pull requests from `api.github.com/repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls` without a token (about 60 requests an hour per address). Draft = in progress (40%), open = in review (80%), merged = done (100%), closed unmerged = skipped. In the VR room an optional fine-grained token (held in memory only) raises the limit and adds check-run status for up to ten open pull requests. Branch prefixes claude/, codex/, copilot/, cursor/, devin/, jules/ name the agent; otherwise the author's login.

## Hand-off

Each task has "Copy brief" (a short prompt to paste into an agent) and, once a repository is set, "Draft issue" (GitHub's new-issue form, prefilled; the user submits it).
